title: 10 best invoicing and payment apps for home-service businesses (2026)
summary: Compare the best invoicing and payment software for contractors that help you get paid faster.
body_markdown:
The best invoicing and payment app for your home-service business depends on your circumstances. Solo plumbers need something very different from large roofing companies running multiple crews with office staff to support them. For example:


- **Topline Pro** is the best invoicing software for most service pros, growing small businesses, and project-based contractors.
- **Square Invoices** may be a better fit for smaller service businesses that just need general marketing, payment processing, and scheduling, rather than a field-service platform.
- **Jobber** makes sense for big shops with a full back-office staff to manage schedules and customer service.


Here’s a breakdown of the 10 best invoicing and payment apps for contractors, including what each one does well, what it costs, and what kind of business it fits best.

## Buyer's guide: What to check in a trial


Some vendors offer trial runs of their software. You should take full advantage of this window. Have them help you set up a mock job from start to finish.


Take the time to build a quote, send an invoice, take payment, and see what happens when a payment is past due. This will help you figure out what features you want to prioritize given your budget.


### Standard payment methods


Look for tools that accept card, ACH, and tap to pay. Remember that some vendors charge higher rates for American Express, tap payments, and Google Pay, or Apple Pay.


Operators that offer high-dollar services may also like to offer buy now, pay later services. Most vendors charge higher fees for those services.


Also check whether you can send an email with a link to an invoice that people can use to pay their bill.


### Processing fees and who pays them


In addition to their monthly subscription fee, most vendors pass along payment processing fees from their providers. You’ll have to look at the fine print on some websites, but they’ll usually tell you a percentage plus a flat transaction fee in the neighborhood of 30 cents per transaction.


A few tenths of a percentage point one way or another may not be a big deal on small jobs. But if you typically deal with bigger reno projects, tiny differences can add up fast.


### Automated reminders


Most tools let you set up automatic reminders that text or email customers to remind them to pay outstanding invoices. If you want that feature, make sure it’s included in the pricing tier you can afford.


### Full monthly cost


Read beyond the advertised base price. Some vendors charge by the number of users you have, while others base their fees on your volume.


Even if they offer unlimited users and volume, you need to make sure the tier you’re looking at has all the features you want. What those features may be depends on your situation:


- **Solo service pros** usually just need a tool that automates or streamlines the steps between delivering a quote and sending the invoice so they can get paid fast.
- **Growing small businesses** have more work to keep straight. They are looking for a way to archive customer records and juggle schedules between multiple operators. They often want their quotes and invoices to carry their branding, and they need a tool that can stay on top of customers who haven’t paid.
- **Route trades** like lawn care, cleaning, and pest control need a tool that offers recurring, automatic billing.
- **Project trades** like roofers, remodelers, and painters need a way to take deposits and bill work as they make progress, rather than in a lump sum at the end.
- **Service call trades** like plumbing, HVAC, and electrical should look for software that makes it easy for techs to finish the job and take payment right then and there.


## The 10 best invoicing apps for contractors


These 10 invoicing apps stand out for contractors who want to send bills faster, take payment easier, and spend less time chasing customers.


### 1. Topline Pro


#### Best for: Owners looking to grow beyond referrals without becoming their own full-time marketer


Topline Pro gives home-service businesses a single tool to handle all their marketing, customer management, job scheduling, and payments.


It’s a strong fit for owner-operators and small-but-growing teams that want help getting more work in the door and handling the administrative side of the business.


Topline Pro’s AI assistant, Sidekick, takes your rough notes about a job and turns them into a branded quote ready to hand to a lead. It automatically converts that quote into an invoice, too. And if a customer is slow to pay, it follows up for you, which saves you time.


Topline Pro also actively seeks out new leads. Prospect Feed trawls Nextdoor looking for users who ask for help with the kinds of services you offer.


Customers can pay by card or ACH through your branded, customer-facing payment portal. If they pay by cash or check instead, it’s simple to mark that in the system.


Topline Pro might be more than you need if all you want is a bare-bones invoice maker. But if you want a website and marketing help, automated customer management tools, and job scheduling, this is a good way to help your business grow faster than word-of-mouth alone will carry you.


#### Key features


- SEO-optimized, custom-built website
- Showcases, which turns your finished work into beautiful portfolio pages on your website
- Automatic social media posting that pulls from job photos you upload to the app’s library
- CRM and customer history
- Prospect Feed for finding local leads on Nextdoor
- QuickBooks integration
- Branded quotes and invoices


#### Pricing


Topline Pro starts at $249 per month when billed annually. Payment processing is 2.90% plus 30 cents for cards and 1.00% for ACH.


### 2. Square Invoices


#### Best for: Contractors who need a simple way to collect payment without a full field-service platform


Square is best known for payments, but there’s a lot more under the hood than you may realize.


Its invoice tool lets you send estimates with multiple options, collect deposits before the work gets started, and turn estimates into invoices after the job is done.


You can also book jobs, send appointment reminders, and set your team’s schedules and track their time.


Square offers Google review monitoring and even a website builder with SEO tools to cover some of your basic marketing needs.


Where Square falls short is the trade-specific stuff. It has schedules and staff management tools, but they aren’t built around dispatch boards and route optimization. It lets you send estimates, but you won’t find pricebooks or job costing calculators. For those reasons, bigger operations are going to get more out of a full field-service platform.


#### Key features


- Google review monitoring
- Team scheduling and time tracking
- Website builder with SEO tools
- Multi-package estimates
- Deposits and payment schedules
- E-signature contracts
- Invoice reporting that shows paid, unpaid, and overdue


#### Pricing


Square Invoices offers a free plan. Its paid tiers start at $49 per month.


Payment processing fees range from 2.4% plus 15 cents for tap or swipe to pay on the premium tier to 3.3% plus 30 cents for online payments on the free tier.


### 3. QuickBooks Online


#### Best for: Businesses that want invoicing tied directly to their books


If you already use QuickBooks for accounting, adding their invoicing tool means estimates, invoices, and payments feed back into your books automatically.


Higher QuickBooks tiers also give you a measure of project management and profitability tracking, which helps you keep a closer eye on your bottom line.


Beyond the back-office accounting tools, QuickBooks now offers a lot more customer-facing tools than it used to. You can now send leads a proposal and e-signature contract, schedule appointments, and manage all your leads and customers in a single Customer Hub.


QuickBooks supports payment by card, ACH, digital wallet, invoice, or tap to pay. Like other tools on this list, it also sends automatic invoice reminders.


However, it is accounting software first. These tools are bolted on, and they fall short of the dispatching tools, equipment service records, route optimization, and other field-service features a more sophisticated operation badly needs.


#### Key features


- Project profitability tracking
- Customer Hub for lead tracking, contracts, and proposals
- Automatic sales tax tracking
- Recurring invoices
- Accountant access so your bookkeeper works off the same records


#### Pricing


QuickBooks Online starts at $38 per month for one user. Payment processing fees range from 1% for ACH payments to 3.5% for keyed-in cards.


### 4. Wave


#### Best for: Solo operators who want basic invoicing and bookkeeping without a big monthly bill


Wave is a lightweight invoicing and accounting tool for very small businesses. Its biggest draw is the free starter plan that generously includes unlimited invoices, estimates, bills, and bookkeeping records.


For a solo operator, Wave is perfect to get you off spreadsheets without taking on a full field-service platform.


Route trades will love the recurring invoices and automated card payments features for their regular customers. Plus, payments feed straight into Wave’s accounting records, which takes some bookkeeping work off your plate.


Wave also lets you upload bank transactions and receipts, then automatically merges and categorizes them.


If you mainly need to send bills, collect payments, and keep the books in order, Wave is the right-sized platform. Large field-service operations running multiple crews should look elsewhere.


#### Key features


- Unlimited invoices, estimates, and bills on the free plan
- Generate deposit requests from estimates
- Automatic late-payment reminders
- Automatic bank transaction imports and categorization
- Unlimited receipt scanning
- Cash flow reporting


#### Pricing


Wave offers a free plan. Its Pro plan is available for $190 a month when billed annually.


Payment processing fees start at 2.9% plus $0 per credit card transaction for the first 10 transactions each month on paid plans. After that there is a 60 cent transaction fee.


### 5. Jobber


#### Best for: Bigger shops with office staff to manage scheduling, quoting, and invoicing


Jobber is a full field-service platform. Beyond its quote and invoicing system, it also handles scheduling, routing, and time tracking for your team. Crews can document their work and expenses, while the back office can pull reports that analyze job profitability.


Every Jobber plan includes a website, but you can add on the platform’s Marketing Suite to also get email campaigns, review tracking, and social posts, and also showcase your work on the website.


You can use Jobber’s built-in AI tools to help you draft social posts, but you’ll still have to review and approve posts before they publish.


Once Jobber has helped you turn leads into clients, it then offers dispatching and scheduling features to help you deliver service. Use the platform to group workers into crews, find schedule openings based on their availability and how far away the job is, then optimize the route they’ll take to get there.


On the job site, field workers can fill out forms, jot notes about the job, and take photos all from the mobile app.


Customers use Jobber’s Client Hub as a centralized place to request work, approve quotes, check appointments, and pay.


Jobber makes the most sense if you have a large roster of techs and plenty of staff back at HQ to manage all of its tools. There’s a lot here that smaller operations that just need invoicing will never touch.


#### Key features


- AI voice and chat for handling tasks and pulling business info
- AI Receptionist for answering clients and booking jobs
- GPS tracking for keeping tabs on multiple crews
- Job costing to monitor profitability
- Marketing Suite for review tracking, email campaigns, and social posts


#### Pricing


Jobber starts at $29 per month, billed annually, for one user on its Core plan. Costs scale from there based on how many people need to use the platform and which tier you’re interested in.


Payment processing fees are between 2.7% and 2.9%, depending on payment method, plus 30 cents per transaction. Like others on this list, ACH payments incur a 1% fee.


### 6. Housecall Pro


#### Best for: Teams that need to know who’s where, who’s available, and where the next job should go


Housecall Pro is a deeply featured home-service platform that makes it easy to keep track of busy crews throughout the day.


It offers a simple drag-and-drop calendar to set and change schedules on the fly. Use live GPS to send the closest available tech when a new call comes in and to see drive times between stops.


Housecall Pro has integrated AI throughout its platform. You can use the CSR AI to field calls, handle customer questions, and book jobs without lifting a finger. The platform offers separate AI assistants for marketing, building reports, and even coaching you on how to improve your business.


On the payment side, techs can have customers tap to pay, swipe their card, or use PayPal, Venmo, or buy-now-pay-later options. For bigger tickets, Housecall Pro offers consumer financing through banking partners.


This is definitely more system than you need if you’re a solo operator who simply wants to send quotes and invoices. However, mid-sized to large businesses may appreciate the feature depth.


#### Key features


- Route optimization based on live traffic data
- CSR AI for customer calls and booking jobs
- Analyst AI for pulling reports and spotting trends
- Good-better-best sales proposals
- Recurring service plans for repeat work
- “On My Way” tracking so customers can follow their tech’s ETA
- Price book for select industries


#### Pricing


Housecall Pro plans start at $59 per month, billed annually, for one user. The Essentials plan is for up to five users, and the Max includes up to eight users.


ACH payments include a 1% charge, while other payment methods range from fees of 2.59% to 4.99%. Tap to pay is an additional $5 per month for each device.


### 7. Joist


#### Best for: Remodelers and GCs that handle long, multi-stage projects


Joist’s target market is general contractors in the project trades who specialize in longer projects where scope can change unexpectedly.


You can use Joist to build an estimate, get it signed in the app, collect a deposit, and set up milestone payments. If a homeowner adds work to your plate halfway through the job, Joist makes it easy to create a change order and add it to the job.


Joist makes heavy use of project and invoice templates so you can quickly ship quotes and estimates for similar job types.


If you’re on Joist’s Run plan, you can schedule visits and keep all your customer information together in a single project under their profile.


Joist is much more project-focused than some of the deeper field-services tools on this list. If you rely heavily on dispatching to get your crews through multiple short service calls a day, you’ll probably want stronger routing and tracking tools than Joist offers. But for high-dollar, multi-stage projects, Joist is more than capable of taking you from estimate to paid invoice.


#### Key features


- Milestone-based payments
- Reusable project templates
- Homeowner financing options
- AI-assisted estimates and invoices


#### Pricing


Joist starts at $8.34 per month, billed annually. It charges 1% for ACH payments. Buy now, pay later services incur a 4.99% fee. Most other payment methods get processed for 3.49% plus 49 cents per transaction.


### 8. ServiceTitan


#### Best for: Large shops that need deep job costing and reporting tools


ServiceTitan is for large commercial contractors tackling huge projects.


It offers all the basic dispatching, scheduling, estimating, invoicing, and fleet tracking tools you’d expect from a full home-service tool. Where it stands out is reporting.


With ServiceTitan, you can track almost everything about your business. Dig into customer service calls and see what your win rate is for different kinds of jobs, then use that data to coach your reps. There’s even a tech scorecard so you can see how much revenue your team generates in the field.


It’s easy to use ServiceTitan’s AI to dig into your data and show historical revenue trends. You can also pull real-time data to track materials and inventory, monitor project progress, and cost jobs.


For a small crew, this is all overkill. But if you’ve got multiple crews out on several massive contracts, ServiceTitan can really shine.


#### Key features


- Detailed job costing across labor, materials, and equipment
- AI-assisted dispatching based on tech skills, location, and job value
- AI Virtual Agents for answering calls and texts and booking work
- Advanced reporting by project, technician, and business unit
- Fleet tracking and maintenance monitoring


#### Pricing


ServiceTitan doesn’t publish its pricing. You’ll have to reach out to sales to get a quote.


### 9. QuoteIQ


#### Best for: Contractors who rely on before-and-after photos to document work


QuoteIQ believes a picture is worth a thousand words. Whether you’re a roofer who needs to document damage or an HVAC tech documenting your inspection checklist, the QuoteIQ Cam makes it easy to take photos, mark them up, and attach them directly to the job profile.


The before-and-after tool is especially well thought out. When you take the “after” photo, QuoteIQ can overlay the original shot on the camera so you can line up the same angle and framing. From there, you can build a side-by-side image, add your logo and labels, and use it in a customer report, estimate, portfolio, or social post.


QuoteIQ makes the most sense for trades where visual proof is part of the work. If you rarely take job photos and mainly need invoices and payments, you probably won’t get as much value from what makes QuoteIQ different.


#### Key features


- Job photos and videos by customer, project, and date
- Custom checklists to work from on the jobsite
- Ghost overlay for before-and-after photos
- Photo annotations for highlighting damage or visually explaining a project to a client


#### Pricing


QuoteIQ’s plans start at $25 per month, billed annually, for one user. Its Max plan comes in at $583.33 for 20 users.


QuoteIQ offers no public pricing on its processing fees.


### 10. FreshBooks


#### Best for: Businesses that bill customers for both time and expenses


FreshBooks is a good fit for contractors who charge time and materials, like plumbers, electricians, and handymen.


Instead of keeping a separate spreadsheet for hours and for receipts, FreshBooks records those things in one place and ties them directly to the project.


FreshBooks also supports recurring invoices and AutoPay, so it works great if you have repeat service customers. Clients can pay by card, ACH, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Affirm, or Afterpay.


FreshBooks is primarily accounting software, so it doesn’t come with the same dispatching and route optimization as the home-service-oriented tools on this list. If you need things like detailed service histories or trade-specific marketing tools, there are better options on this list.


#### Key features


- Time tracking that feeds directly into invoices
- Expense tracking for materials, mileage, and other costs
- AutoPay and recurring invoices
- Project profitability tracking
- Receipt capture


#### Pricing


FreshBooks plans start at $181.33 per year. However, please note that Freshbooks is currently listing all these prices as a limited time offer, without a clear end date for the sale. Its processing fees range from 1% for ACH payments to 6% for buy now, pay later options.


## How to get paid faster


Here are a few ways you can tweak your workflow to get paid faster:


- **Invoice on site:** Don’t wait until you’re back at the office to send an invoice. Use a tool that lets customers tap or swipe a card, or use something like Google Pay or Apple Pay, before you get back in the truck.
- **Collect deposits:** Always get money up front on bigger jobs so you aren’t left waiting for the full balance at the end. With Topline Pro, as soon as a customer signs a quote, it will take them to a payment screen for the first milestone (usually a deposit).
- **Offer text-to-pay:** Not everybody checks their email daily. Sometimes you can get a more immediate response if you let customers pay straight from their phone.
- **Automate reminders:** Software lets you set follow-ups once, then it automatically chases those overdue invoices for you.
- **Use the right tools:** The right invoicing app helps you get paid without chasing customers and cuts down the time you spend doing the books at the dinner table.
